title: To-day Thy Mercy Calls Us
description: To-day Thy Mercy Calls Us in Tonic Solfa to ANGEL'S STORY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Oswald Allen wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 50.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ANGEL'S STORY; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: To day Thy mer-cy calls us To wash a-way our sin. How-ev-er great our tres-pass, What-ev-er we have been; How-ev-er long from mer-cy Our hearts have turned a-way, Thy pre-cious blood can cleanse us And make us white to day.

lines: Thy precious blood can cleanse us
No question will be asked us
What should we do without Thee
When heart and eye run o’er?
When all things seem against us,
We know one gate is open,
One ear will hear our prayer.

licence: Public domain: Oswald Allen died in 1878.
credits: Words by Oswald Allen (1816–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ANGEL'S STORY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
